name: Ten-year data centre power and modular gas generation retrospective (2016–2026)
aliases: Ten-year data centre power and modular gas generation retrospective (2016–2026)
principle: A ten-year retrospective of data-centre power plants, gas engines and small modular generation, assembled from dated project, technology, vendor and cost evidence with sources and dollar years where published.

process_steps.name: Data centre IT load and cooling

performance.metric: Operational history — IEA reports transmission build time and grid-component lead times
performance.basis: New transmission lines can take four to eight years in advanced economies; wait times for transformers and cables have doubled in the past three years; gas turbine deliveries now face lead times of several years, potentially delaying commissioning beyond 2030.

performance.metric: Operational history — Singapore DC-CFA2 makes green-energy and grid-linked siting a condition of new capacity
performance.basis: IMDA and EDB launched DC-CFA2 on 1 December 2025 for at least 200 MW of new capacity; applicants must use green energy pathways, and future scalability is said to depend on regional renewable electricity imports and ASEAN grid interconnection initiatives; Singapore runs a biomethane sandbox.

performance.metric: Reliability — planned data centre projects at risk of delay from grid constraints
performance.basis: IEA Energy and AI (2025) executive summary: unless risks are addressed, around 20% of planned data centre projects could be at risk of delays; long and complex grid connection queues

performance.metric: Operational history — Google and Kairos Power sign 500 MW multi-plant advanced nuclear PPA
performance.basis: Announced 14 October 2024: first corporate agreement in the US for multiple deployments of a single advanced reactor design; first deployment by 2030; plants sited in relevant service territories to supply Google data centres; Kairos founded 2016; NRC issued a construction permit for the Hermes demonstration reactor in 2023, the first non-water-cooled reactor approved for construction in the US in

performance.metric: Operational history — IEA projects first SMRs online around 2030 and tech-sector SMR financing above 20 GW
performance.basis: IEA Energy and AI (2025): first SMRs come online around 2030; technology companies have plans to finance more than 20 GW of SMRs; natural gas expands by 175 TWh to meet data centre demand, notably in the United States.

performance.metric: Reliability — GE Vernova stated reliability for data-centre gas turbine fleet
performance.basis: Vendor claim on GE Vernova data-centre page; no measurement basis or period given

performance.metric: Operational history — Digital Realty joins EirGrid DS3 dynamic frequency balancing with nine Dublin data centres
performance.basis: Enel X case study: when grid frequency drops below 50 Hz, Digital Realty's nine highly connected Irish data centres draw power from their batteries, reducing grid demand almost instantaneously; the collaboration is stated to avoid over 24,000 tonnes of CO2 emissions. No date is given on the page.

performance.metric: Reliability — UPS failure as root cause of major power-related outages
performance.basis: Uptime Institute Data Center Resiliency Survey 2026, Figure 10 (n=129): UPS failure 39%, utility transfer switch failure 34%, generator failure 28%, PDU failure 19%, A/B transfer switch failure 16%, controls failure 8%, single-corded IT failure 16%

performance.metric: Reliability — lithium-ion UPS batteries as contributing factor in data-centre fires
performance.basis: Uptime Institute Annual outage analysis 2026: frequency of major fires at data centres has increased gradually in recent years, with lithium-ion batteries in UPS systems a clear contributing factor; report cautions the rise may partly reflect rapid build-out of new facilities

performance.metric: Operational history — Uptime reports equipment shortage driving substitute and second-user gensets
performance.basis: Annual outage analysis 2026: extremely high demand has created a global shortage of generators, transformers, switchgear, UPS systems and other subsystems; some owners buy second-user equipment or source substitute components from suppliers without a proven data centre track record, which the report says has contributed to several failures. Operators are adapting investment toward automation and c

performance.metric: Reliability — generator failure as root cause of major power-related outages
performance.basis: Uptime Institute Data Center Resiliency Survey 2026, Figure 10 (n=129); UPS failure 39% and utility transfer switch failure 34% ranked above generator failure

performance.metric: Reliability — grid failure effects on on-site standby power
performance.basis: Uptime Institute Annual outage analysis 2026: grid failures should not cause a data centre outage assuming on-site primary power, but can affect availability of on-site power through a failed power switchover or disruptions to diesel supply triggered by the grid failure

performance.metric: Operational history — Singapore Green Data Centre Roadmap 2024 sets near-term capacity and efficiency targets
performance.basis: IMDA launched the roadmap in June 2024, targeting at least 300 MW of new data centre capacity in the near term; DC-CFA2 from December 2025 requires PUE of 1.25 or better at 100% IT load, Green Mark for DC Platinum 2024, IT equipment meeting SS 715:2025, and at least 50% of new capacity powered by eligible green energy pathways.

performance.metric: Reliability — cooling as primary cause of most recent impactful data centre outage
performance.basis: Uptime Institute Global Data Center Survey 2025, Figure 4 (n=96): power 45%, cooling 14%, IT systems 11%, network 9%, fire suppression 6%, fire 5%, colocation 4%, unknown 2%, third-party 2%, information security 1% (figures rounded)

performance.metric: Operational history — Uptime identifies higher voltages and on-site storage as emerging rack-power risks
performance.basis: Annual outage analysis 2026: in the years ahead operators face higher rack densities, higher voltages, lower grid reliability and increased on-site energy storage; these challenges may add to outage risk and highlight the need for policies, training and on-site expertise.

performance.metric: Reliability — PDU failure as root cause of major power-related outages
performance.basis: Uptime Institute Data Center Resiliency Survey 2026, Figure 10 (n=129): PDU failure 19%, single-corded IT device failure 16%; report notes PDU, transfer switching and single-corded IT outages increased significantly versus the early-2025 survey

performance.metric: Operational history — Uptime reports a shift toward distributed resiliency and Tier III for AI sites
performance.basis: Annual outage analysis 2026: distributed resiliency — spreading active workloads across several locations — reduces single-site failure impact but increases synchronisation cost and complexity; some AI training sites were built at speed with crypto-mining-style low-resiliency designs, while more recent evidence suggests a trend toward higher facility resiliency such as Tier III.

performance.metric: Reliability — operators reporting an impactful outage in the past three years
performance.basis: Uptime Institute Global Data Center Survey 2025 (n=754), reported in Annual outage analysis 2026: series 74% (2020), 69% (2021), 60% (2022), 55% (2023), 53% (2024), 50% (2025); lowest since 2020

performance.metric: Reliability — outage classified serious or severe
performance.basis: Uptime Institute Annual outage analysis 2026: proportion of serious/severe incidents 10% in 2025 versus 9% in 2024; fifth consecutive year of declining per-site outage frequency, but pace of improvement slowed

performance.metric: Operational history — IEA publishes 2024 fuel mix for electricity physically consumed by data centres
performance.basis: IEA Energy and AI (2025), Energy supply for AI: generation supplying data centres grows from 460 TWh in 2024 to over 1,000 TWh in 2030 and 1,300 TWh in 2035 (Base Case). 2024 mix: coal about 30% (largest), renewables about 27%, natural gas 26%, nuclear 15%. Renewables grow at an annual average 22% between 2024 and 2030 and meet nearly 50% of growth; some capacity is financed through PPAs with tech

performance.metric: Operational history — IEA projects the first SMRs entering the data-centre supply mix after 2030
performance.basis: IEA Energy supply for AI: after 2030 SMRs enter the mix; hyperscalers are key corporate backers; in the United States technology companies have plans to finance more than 20 GW of SMRs. CO2 from data-centre electricity generation peaks around 320 Mt CO2 by 2030 then declines to around 300 Mt by 2035 in the Base Case.

performance.metric: Operational history — Singapore requires at least 50% green-energy pathways for DC-CFA2 capacity
performance.basis: DC-CFA2 launched 1 December 2025 requires selected applicants to power at least 50% of new capacity through eligible green energy pathways: biomethane, low-carbon ammonia, low-carbon hydrogen, novel fuel cells with carbon capture and storage, or vertical building-integrated/building-applied photovoltaics.

performance.metric: Operational history — IEA quantifies AI data centre scale and local concentration
performance.basis: IEA Energy and AI (2025): a typical AI-focused data centre consumes as much electricity as 100,000 households and the largest under construction will consume 20 times as much; global investment in data centres nearly doubled since 2022 to half a trillion dollars in 2024; an AI-focused data centre is 10 times more capital-intensive than an aluminium smelter, making curtailment very costly; 50% of U

performance.metric: Operational history — Uptime flags AI resiliency as an open question
performance.basis: Annual outage analysis 2026: very large AI training and hyperscale sites are not yet a focus because most only recently came into operation; AI training facilities repeatedly stop and start model runs to address IT component failures; major power or cooling failures could prove expensive due to lost work even if end users are unaffected; there have been near-miss incidents that could have caused m

performance.metric: Reliability — operators saying most recent major outage cost more than USD 100,000
performance.basis: Uptime Institute 2025 annual survey, reported in Annual outage analysis 2026: 57% say most recent major outage cost more than $100,000; one in five (20%) say more than $1 million for the second year in a row; dollar year not stated

performance.metric: Operational history — IEA sets out flexibility options and their cost constraint
performance.basis: IEA Energy and AI (2025): grid connection queues are long and complex; an AI-focused data centre is 10 times more capital-intensive than an aluminium smelter so curtailing operations to provide flexibility is very costly; many data centres operate with spare server capacity, and regulators could incentivise use of that capacity or of backup generation and storage; grid operators could incentivise

performance.metric: Operational history — IEA sensitivity cases show queue-driven fuel mix differences
performance.basis: IEA Energy supply for AI: in the Lift-Off Case global electricity generation for data centres approaches 2,000 TWh by 2035, 45% above Base Case, but long grid connection queues mean most additional growth beyond 2030 is met by fossil fuels; in that case nearly 50% of additional generation to 2030 comes from fossil fuels.

performance.metric: Operational history — Enel X and Digital Realty use UPS batteries for EirGrid frequency response
performance.basis: Under EirGrid's DS3 programme, Digital Realty's nine Irish data centres draw on batteries when frequency falls below 50 Hz, turning idle backup into a grid-balancing asset; no date stated on the page.

performance.metric: Reliability — near-miss grid incidents linked to large data centres
performance.basis: Uptime Institute Annual outage analysis 2026: there have already been some near-miss incidents that could have resulted in major grid outages; mitigation measures are being introduced but systemic failure likelihood appears to have increased in recent years

performance.metric: Operational history — Uptime publishes the eighth Annual Outage Analysis
performance.basis: Keynote Report 201, May 2026, authors Douglas Donnellan, Andy Lawrence and Rose Weinschenk. It draws on the Data Center Resiliency Survey 2026 (Feb-Mar 2026, >450 operator and 500 vendor respondents), the Global Data Center Survey 2025 (Q2 2025, >800 operators) and public outage reports from 2025 and Q1 2026.

performance.metric: Operational history — Outage frequency declines for the fifth consecutive year but gains slow
performance.basis: Annual outage analysis 2026: per-site outage frequency is declining for the fifth consecutive year, but the pace of improvement has slowed and around one in 10 respondents still say their last outage had serious or severe impacts; failures increasingly involve complex interactions, external connectivity and grid constraints rather than a single point of failure.
